name: Soft landing, full current
description: Your soft-landing optics from arc 1 (Charges) are built in. With a real ion current the braked ions crowd together and repel each other: the slower they get, the stronger the space charge, and the beam blows up just before the target. At least 90 % must still land gently on the target. Add a few charges.

reality.represents: Soft landing with an intense ion beam

remarks.line: Space charge grows as the beam slows
remarks.detail: The same current packed into a slower beam is a denser charge: braked ions crowd and blow up just before the target.

remarks.line: A beam of a few particles
remarks.detail: A dozen or so particles stand for a beam of billions: each carries the charge of many (its mass and energy scaled alike, so that its own path is unchanged), so their repulsion matches an intense beam's. The spreads are a fixed sample of the beam's distribution, the same every time.
The target is a detector: what the ions do on arrival is not modelled.

Everything is symmetric about the plane z = 0, so the particle never leaves it. A real beam also has a width across the plane, where the same fields act differently (focusing in the plane can defocus across it).
